dedupe_keys.name: reconstructing historical housing data using kriging interpolation and zonal statistics

description: Reconstructing Historical Housing Data Using Kriging Interpolation and Zonal Statistics is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Shuang Tian et al. Administrative boundaries in the United States frequently shift due to population growth and redistricting, complicating longitudinal analyses of census-based socio-economic data. In California, the number and configuration of census tracts and block groups have changed substantially between 1990 and 2020, often resulting in misaligned or missing historical data, especially for variables such as housing value. Coverage: national (US); published in 2026. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The paper's page was read, but no repository address could be taken from its machine-readable metadata, so the record links to the article, whose Data Records section names where the data sit. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support building-stock, asset and facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
